parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.stem:
The following table lists the solubilities of the hydroxides and carbonates of some of the Group 2 elements, $\mathbf{M}$, at $25^{\circ}\text{C}$.

| element $\mathbf{M}$ | solubility / $\text{mol dm}^{-3}$ |  |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
|  | $\text{M(OH)}_2$ | $\text{MCO}_3$ |
| $\text{Mg}$ | $2.0 \times 10^{-4}$ | $1.5 \times 10^{-3}$ |
| $\text{Ca}$ | $1.5 \times 10^{-2}$ | $1.3 \times 10^{-4}$ |
| $\text{Sr}$ | $3.4 \times 10^{-2}$ | $7.4 \times 10^{-5}$ |
| $\text{Ba}$ | $1.5 \times 10^{-1}$ | $9.1 \times 10^{-5}$ |
parts.text: Explain why the solubility of the Group 2 hydroxides, $\text{M(OH)}_2$, increases down the group.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Suggest a reason for the general decrease in the solubility of the Group 2 carbonates, $\text{MCO}_3$, down the group.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text:
When carbon dioxide is passed through a saturated solution of calcium hydroxide (limewater), a white precipitate of calcium carbonate is formed.

Use the data in the table to deduce, for **each** of Mg, Sr and Ba, whether or not a saturated solution of its hydroxide could also be used to test for carbon dioxide. Explain your answer. No calculations are required.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Calculate the value of the solubility product, $K_{\text{sp}}$, of magnesium hydroxide at $25^{\circ}\text{C}$.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: State what would be observed if a few drops of a saturated solution of barium hydroxide are added to a saturated solution of barium carbonate. Explain your answer.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The equation for the formation of the gaseous hydroxide ion is shown.

$$\frac{1}{2}\text{H}_2(\text{g}) + \frac{1}{2}\text{O}_2(\text{g}) + \text{e}^- \rightarrow \text{OH}^-(\text{g}) \qquad \Delta H = \Delta H_{\text{f}}^{\ominus}(\text{OH}^-(\text{g}))$$

Use data in the table and from the *Data Booklet* to calculate $\Delta H_{\text{f}}^{\ominus}(\text{OH}^-(\text{g}))$. You might find it useful to construct a Born-Haber cycle.

| enthalpy change | $\Delta H^{\ominus}/\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| atomisation of $\text{Mg(s)}$ | $+148$ |
| formation of $\text{Mg(OH)}_2\text{(s)}$ | $-925$ |
| lattice energy of $\text{Mg(OH)}_2\text{(s)}$ | $-2993$ |
